attempts.user_message:
Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-gvjsbv9i/call-7e786a449f12406ead97c5bbe0245532/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for name in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','pypdfium2','PIL']:
 print(name, importlib.util.find_spec(name))
for name in ['pdftoppm','pdftotext','pdfinfo','gs','python3']:
 print(name, shutil.which(name))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGES',len(r.pages))
print('METADATA',r.metadata)
texts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages):
 t=p.extract_text()
 texts.append(f'\\n\\n=== PAGE {i+1} ===\\n'+t)
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i+1:02d}.txt').write_text(t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(texts))
print(''.join(texts[:3]))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from statistics import NormalDist
from math import log
z=[NormalDist().inv_cdf((i+1)/5) for i in range(4)]
q0=[-3,-1,1,3]
scale=sum(q/zv for q,zv in zip(q0,z))/4
q=[v/scale for v in q0]
fitted_sd=sum(qv/zv for qv,zv in zip(q,z))/4
print('Illustrative ordered non-Gaussian quantile vector:',q)
print('Normal quantile target:',z)
print('Paper fitted SD:',fitted_sd)
print('KL against a unit-SD normal:',log(fitted_sd)+(1/(fitted_sd*fitted_sd)-1)/2)
print('Even independent unit-variance rewards have discounted sum variance (gamma=.99):')
for n in [1,10,100,1000]:
 print(n,(1-.99**(2*n))/(1-.99**2))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an identifiable audience in distributional reinforcement learning and continuous control. A time-dependent critic target and exploration derived from critic predictions are useful ideas to investigate. :codex-file-citation{path="/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b10/review-experiment-gvjsbv9i/call-7e786a449f12406ead97c5bbe0245532/manuscript.pdf" purpose="source"}

The main evaluation covers eight environments with ten random seeds. Including DPPO and an ablation without the exploration bonus provides useful evidence about the components; these distributional variants share the same critic architecture.
Figure 2 and Algorithm 1 make the overall procedure understandable. Table 2 also provides an interesting practical observation about quantile count and quantile crossing.
weaknesses: Required: Repair the central theoretical justification (Theorem 1 and Equations 6–8). A CLT for normalized, long, undiscounted sums does not establish approximate normality or a linear variance schedule for finite, state-conditional discounted returns. Even independent rewards with variance v give discounted-sum variance v(1−gamma^(2n))/(1−gamma²), rather than nv. The initialization of variance with R_cur² is also not derived from the theorem: shifting rewards by a constant can change this quantity without changing fixed-horizon return variance. Provide a valid justification for the implemented setting or explicitly frame and evaluate the schedule as a heuristic. This is a substantive failure of the current evidence criterion.

Required: Correct the argument following Equation 4. Shrinking the quantiles of one sampled Bellman target does not imply that the full return distribution must have variance increasing with timestep. Mixing over random successor states and rewards contributes additional variance. Standard distributional Bellman updates can represent decreasing remaining-return variance, so the claimed contradiction motivating the method is incorrect.

Required: Strengthen or narrow the empirical claims about return distributions. Figure 1 compares learned critic outputs with fitted Gaussians, rather than comparing actual sampled returns with Gaussians. Table 1 pools returns across episodes without establishing the state-conditional distributions relevant to the critic. It also reports approximately linear decreases in standard deviation, whereas Equation 8 makes variance linear. These observations do not validate the proposed distributional model. Conditional rollout measurements across representative states would address this gap.

Required: Correct the interpretation of the exploration statistic (Equation 11). Its KL divergence compares two Gaussians with identical means and therefore measures disagreement between fitted scales; it is not a distance between the learned quantile distribution and a Gaussian. Non-Gaussian quantile configurations can receive zero divergence. No measurements establish the claimed connection to insufficient visitation or improved critic accuracy. Moreover, when R_t/l is negative, the clipping rule makes the bonus negative and independent of KL, which matters for the negative-return environments shown. Resolve this behavior and either validate the proposed mechanism or narrow the interpretation to heuristic reward shaping.

Required: Resolve ambiguities in the implemented algorithm. Equation 10 uses prediction-minus-target residuals with the weighting convention for target-minus-prediction, reversing the intended quantile asymmetry. The DPPO target described on page 6 omits gamma. Clarify whether these are transcription errors or the actual implementations. Also specify the return target, termination and truncation handling, updates of R_cur and l_cur, and task-specific values and selection procedures for N, alpha, and sigma_min; the supplied manuscript does not provide these sufficiently.

Required: Improve experimental attribution and reporting. Scalar PPO uses a 64×64 critic while the distributional methods use 512×512 critics, so its comparison confounds the proposed changes with critic capacity. A comparable-capacity PPO control is needed to attribute those gains. Clarify whether plotted returns exclude the intrinsic bonus, and reconcile the Figure 3 caption's standard deviations with the text's standard errors. The claim of best performance in every domain also needs qualification: DPPO appears higher at the end of BipedalWalker-v3, and several differences are small relative to the displayed variability.

Optional: Sensitivity studies for the variance schedule and comparisons with other exploration bonuses would help practitioners understand when the approach is useful. Additional actor-critic backbones would broaden the findings, but are unnecessary if the claims remain scoped to the evaluated PPO setting.
